summary_md: **Artificial Intelligence Papers ([@SciFi](https://x.com/SciFi/status/2115989533627994374))** shares *When Retrieval Is Not Enough* ([arXiv 2610.36308](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36308)), which separates retrieval from answering in memory agents and finds obsolete facts drive many errors even when the update was retrieved (NeurIPS 2026 PALM workshop).

referenced_urls.title: When Retrieval Is Not Enough: Obsolete Facts in Agent Memory

relevance: Memory staleness as a distinct agent failure mode.

media.description: Image of the paper's abstract text.
media.ocr_text: Memory-agent benchmarks often collapse retrieval and answer generation into one score, making it hard to tell whether a failure comes from missing an update or from not using an update that was already retrieved. We examine this distinction on the single-hop FactConsolidation task of MemoryAgentBench. With Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on 6K-history BM25 accuracy drops from 45% to 32% when the retrieved evidence budget grows from 64 to 512 tokens, even though a gold-assisted post-hoc audit finds the newest statement in every retrieved set. Most of the errors occur on questions that also contain an obsolete statement version. Under a frozen prompt and equal four-statement evidence size, replacing one unrelated statement with the obsolete competing statement reduces accuracy from 100% to 44.6% for Qwen2.5 and from 100% to 87.8% for Qwen3-14B, with all 50 harmful paired flips classified as stale.
